name: openstrawberry

scripts.release: pnpm verify:config && pnpm release:preflight && pnpm check && pnpm test && pnpm build && electron-builder --publish never --config.mac.notarize=true && pnpm checksums && pnpm verify:artifacts
scripts.comment:release:unsigned: The same chain with notarisation off, for a deliberate unsigned prerelease. It is not a weaker gate wearing a different name: every step still runs, and both release:preflight and verify:artifacts refuse to proceed unless OPENSTRAWBERRY_ALLOW_UNSIGNED is set in the environment, which nothing here does.
scripts.release:unsigned: pnpm verify:config && pnpm release:preflight && pnpm check && pnpm test && pnpm build && electron-builder --publish never && pnpm checksums && pnpm verify:artifacts

comment:dependencies: One entry, and it had to earn it. Everything declared here is packaged into the asar, so React, React DOM, and Lucide stay out: Vite bundles them into the renderer, and listing them again shipped fifty source maps of never-executed code in every artifact. electron-updater is different because src/main/update-transport.ts imports it at runtime - without it in the package the update channel resolves nothing. It costs sixteen packages (its own tree: builder-util-runtime, js-yaml, fs-extra, semver, and their dependencies), and unlike the renderer libraries every one of them actually runs.
comment:build: The mac block builds a DMG and a ZIP from one universal app. The DMG is what a person downloads; the ZIP is what the updater downloads, because Squirrel.Mac can only apply an update delivered as a ZIP - a mac channel shipping only a DMG publishes metadata pointing at a file it cannot install. Comment keys live out here: electron-builder validates its own blocks against a schema, and pnpm verify:config fails an unrecognised option inside one.
